answer: Submissions that land within 45 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. The kernel detector writes to horizon, and wharf makes public every merge. A farm scripting its whole swarm fires them together, which means the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 168 aliases out burns the operator real scheduling effort per key. That is 30 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
